what_happened: Cross-referencing specs/archive/497.../issues.jsonl and specs/archive/450.../issues.jsonl against orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's Batch Gate Deferral emission code located a precise, narrowly-scoped composer defect (final-phase-only directive text) directly implicated by 3 primary-source issue-log entries, avoiding a broader/costlier rebuild of already-working Mechanism A/B or .gate-lock machinery.

validate-artifact.sh --strict caught two authoring defects in the first draft of plans/01_full-gate-batch-concurrency.md before return: backtick-leading wrapped continuation lines in two Files-to-modify blocks (read as prose, silently dropping no path but flagged), and three Tier Justifications that named a hand-picked suite subset narrower than suite_selection_select's own closure for the same touched paths. Both were fixed in place; the under-verification finding also drove Phase 3's tier up from interface to full, which is the honest tier for an edit to verify-deploy.sh itself.

Premise re-validation found a surface the research report did not name: context/formats/plan-format.md's '### Batch-aware deferral' subsection carries the SAME final-phase-only scoping in prose ('the final phase's own in-dispatch obligation narrows...') as the composer does in code. Fixing only the composer (research Recommendation 1) would have left the tier-declaration contract contradicting the mechanism. Phase 2 of the plan exists solely because of this check.
